result.topic_en: Gauss evaluates the integral of 1/sqrt(1 - x^2 cos^2 φ) from 0 to π via a series of cosine powers, identifies the result with the constant term of a cosine-multiple expansion, and derives a general theorem linking that constant term to the arithmetic-geometric mean of the reciprocals of the maximum and minimum values.
result.transcription:
13
Sit $\varphi$ angulus indefinitus, eritque valor integralis $\int\cos\varphi^2\partial\varphi$,
a $\varphi=0$ usque ad $\varphi=\pi$, ut vulgo notum est, $=\frac{1}{2}\pi$; eodem modo
fit valor integralis $\int\cos\varphi^4\partial\varphi$ inter eosdem limites $=\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{3}{4}\pi$; va
lor integralis $\int\cos\varphi^6\partial\varphi=\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{3}{4}\cdot\frac{5}{6}\pi$ etc. — denique ut sponte patet
$\int\partial\varphi=\pi$. Hinc perspicuum est, valorem integralis $\int\partial\varphi\times(1+\frac{1}{2}x^2\cos\varphi^2+\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{3}{4}x^4\cos\varphi^4+\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{3}{4}\cdot\frac{5}{6}x^6\cos\varphi^6+\text{etc.})$ sive huius $\int\frac{\partial\varphi}{\sqrt{(1-xx\cos\varphi^2)}}$
fieri $=\pi y$, si sumatur a $\varphi=0$ usque ad $\varphi=\pi$, spectando quan
titatem $x$ tamquam constantem.
Quodsi functio $\frac{1}{\sqrt{(1-xx\cos\varphi^2)}}$ in seriem talem evolvi supponatur,
$P+2Q\cos2\varphi+2R\cos4\varphi+2S\cos6\varphi+\text{etc.}$, ita ut coëfficientes
$P, Q, R, S$ etc. a sola $x$ pendeant: valor integralis supra traditi com
pletus erit $P\varphi+Q\sin2\varphi+\frac{1}{2}R\sin4\varphi+\frac{1}{3}S\sin6\varphi+\text{etc.}+\text{Const.}$
adeoque valor intra limites ante allatos, $=P\varphi$, unde $y=P$.
Jam observamus, quum sit $\frac{1}{y}=M(1+x,1-x)$ fieri quoque $\frac{1}{y}$
$=M(1,\sqrt{(1-xx)})$. Hinc facillime derivatur sequens theorema gene
ralius: Si expressio talis $\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{(\beta-\gamma\cos\varphi^2)}}=W$ in seriem secundum
cosinus angulorum $2\varphi, 4\varphi, 6\varphi$ etc. progredientem evolvatur cuius
terminus constans designetur per $P$; valores maximus et minimus ipsi
us $W$ autem (puta $\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{(\beta-\gamma)}}$ et $\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{\beta}}$) denotentur per $v, v'$: erit $\frac{1}{P}$ me
dium arithmetico-geometricum inter $\frac{1}{v}$ et $\frac{1}{v'}$. Proxime quidem
ratiocinia praecedentia pro eo tantummodo casu valent, ubi $\gamma$ est
quantitas positiva: sed facillime ad eum quoque casum extenduntur
ubi $\gamma$ est negativus. In hocce enim casu fit $W=\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{(\beta-\gamma+\gamma\cos\psi^2)}}$
ponendo $\psi=90^\circ-\varphi$; unde $\frac{1}{P}$ med. inter $\frac{\sqrt{\beta}}{\alpha}$ et $\frac{\sqrt{(\beta-\gamma)}}{\alpha}$. Ut supra.
Ceterum nullo negotio patet, idem theorema sine ulla mutatione etiam
ad expressiones tales $\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{(\beta+\gamma\cos\varphi)}}$ extendi, puta ut $\frac{1}{\text{Term. Const.}}$ fiat
$=M\left(\frac{1}{\text{valor max.}},\frac{1}{\text{valor minim.}}\right)=M\left(\frac{\sqrt{(\beta-\gamma)}}{\alpha},\frac{\sqrt{(\beta+\gamma)}}{\alpha}\right)$; huius modi

General theorem: the reciprocal of the constant Fourier term of α/√(β−γcos²φ) is the AGM of the reciprocals of its maximum and minimum values
Extension to negative γ by the substitution ψ = 90° − φ
